title: Governed handover when someone leaves
author: shweta
desc:
Somebody leaves the company. This workflow finds the changes nobody approved, reports everything the departing user owns across Leads, Deals, Contacts and Accounts, reassigns the whole book in one governed batch, and closes with per-record evidence of what actually happened.

THE PART NOBODY ELSE DOES. An offboarding is exactly when ungoverned edits matter most. In the days before somebody goes, their records may have been edited by hand - by them, by a manager, by an automation nobody remembers configuring - and then a bulk reassignment moves the whole book at once. scan_changes already finds changes with no approval behind them. plan_handover already finds what this person owns. Node 10 intersects the two: of the records about to be handed over, how many were edited outside the airlock? That number raises the approval tier at node 11. A clean book moves on a routine approval. A book that has been quietly edited gets escalated, because it should be. No other workflow can ask this, because no other module has scan_changes.

SEVENTEEN NODES, FIVE OF THEM PURE LOGIC. Intake: verify_connection names any missing scope before a read is attempted; list_users runs with AllUsers so a leaver who is already deactivated is still visible; a transform then checks both users - both exist, the receiving user is active, they are not the same person - and refuses in pure logic rather than failing three nodes later. Review: scan_changes, plan_handover, then four read-only COQL reads, one per module, that fetch the leaver's book by owner. The join at node 10 is BY RECORD, on module and id, across all four modules - not by owner, and not on one module. Node 11 sets the tier, node 12 fails closed. Commit: apply_handover runs only if the guard passed. Evidence: reconcile_writes settles any write Zoho never confirmed, verify_ledger checks the chain, custody_report gives a per-record verdict, and a final transform decides whether the run may call itself finished.

PLAN THEN APPLY. An approval binds to the inputs a human saw, not to the records they point at. plan_handover fingerprints the exact set it is about to move. apply_handover re-reads that set, re-hashes it, and REFUSES if anything moved in between - so a record edited between review and execution stops the write rather than being swept up in it. A CRM has no undo, and this is the gap ordinary automation leaves open.

Every step produces a signed receipt and the run carries an integrity root over all seventeen nodes. The change ledger is hash-chained: each entry carries the fingerprint of the one before it, so editing or removing an entry breaks every link after it.

Live execution is OFF by default. Dry-run works anywhere; firing this workflow for real requires an operator to enable Studio DAG live runs under Studio -> Settings -> Live Execution. That toggle is the human gate on this path, and the setting is signed on save.

HONEST LIMITS, ALL OF THEM. The approval tier at node 11 is REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED - the station is the approval authority, and reaching a real second approver needs team_approval and a mesh of separate approvers that a solo station cannot form. The risk join sees what scan_changes sees: ungoverned EDITS. A record deleted or merged in the Zoho UI leaves nothing to poll, so an overlap count of zero is not proof of a clean book. Scan coverage starts at the earliest entry in the live ledger chain; the chain rotates and sealed archives are not read. custody_report detects THAT a record diverged, not how many times, because Zoho exposes no per-field history. The ledger is tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof. Record ids go to a file, because receipts redact identifiers. Closed deals are excluded from a handover unless you ask for them.

EVIDENCE SCOPING, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. The risk join at node 10 covers all four modules, because a one-module risk assessment would miss most of the book. The custody report at node 16 covers LEADS ONLY - custody_report takes one module per call and caps at 500 records. Contacts, Accounts and Deals are covered by the ledger check at node 15, which proves the chain is intact and that every write was recorded, but does not produce a per-record verdict for those three modules. Node 17 says so in its own output rather than reporting a clean run it cannot evidence.

A KNOWN CONSTRAINT. plan_handover and apply_handover resolve both users against Zoho's ActiveConfirmedUsers list, so a leaver who has already been deactivated cannot currently be handed over - the two nodes will report the user as unmatched. Node 3 catches this in pure logic and names it, instead of surfacing it as a confusing failure at node 5. Handing over BEFORE deactivating the account works today.

Trigger contract: supply from_user and to_user as email addresses of Zoho CRM users.

Dependencies: requires shweta/zoho-crm v0.9.1 or later, with the zoho vault entry configured (client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, token_url, instance_url). Run zoho.verify_connection first - it names any missing scope and which commands it blocks. [contest:2026Q3]

nodes.code:
# Node 3. Pure logic, so a bad user pair is caught before any effect node runs.
# A live run of the 4-node workflow failed at plan_handover with "No active
# user matches ..." - a good error that arrived after two nodes had executed.
#
# Tolerates None everywhere: at plan time no effect node has stored an output,
# so `users` arrives as None and every field below resolves to a miss.
src = input.get("users") or {}
rows = src.get("users") or []
want_from = str(input.get("from_user") or "").strip().lower()
want_to = str(input.get("to_user") or "").strip().lower()
problems = []

def pick(want):
    if not want:
        return None
    hits = []
    for u in rows:
        if not isinstance(u, dict):
            continue
        if want == str(u.get("id") or "").strip().lower():
            return u
        email = str(u.get("email") or "").strip().lower()
        name = str(u.get("full_name") or "").strip().lower()
        if want == email or want == name:
            hits.append(u)
    if len(hits) == 1:
        return hits[0]
    return None

leaver = pick(want_from)
taker = pick(want_to)

if not want_from:
    problems.append("ctx.from_user is empty")
elif leaver is None:
    problems.append("from_user " + want_from + " matches no user, or matches more than one")
if not want_to:
    problems.append("ctx.to_user is empty")
elif taker is None:
    problems.append("to_user " + want_to + " matches no user, or matches more than one")

from_status = str((leaver or {}).get("status") or "").strip().lower()
to_status = str((taker or {}).get("status") or "").strip().lower()

# The RECEIVING user must be active. Handing a book to a deactivated user
# would leave it owned by nobody who can work it, which is the condition
# hygiene_scan reports as orphaned.
if taker is not None and to_status != "active":
    problems.append("to_user is not active (status " + (to_status or "unknown") + ")")

# The DEPARTING user being deactivated is the normal case for an offboarding,
# so it is a finding, not a failure. It is also a sharper risk signal: a
# deactivated owner whose records are still being edited is worse than an
# active one. Node 11 reads from_deactivated for exactly that.
from_deactivated = leaver is not None and from_status != "active"

same_user = (leaver is not None and taker is not None
             and str(leaver.get("id")) == str(taker.get("id")))
if same_user:
    problems.append("from_user and to_user are the same person")

output = {
    "ok": not problems,
    "problems": problems,
    "from_found": leaver is not None,
    "to_found": taker is not None,
    "from_id": str((leaver or {}).get("id") or ""),
    "to_id": str((taker or {}).get("id") or ""),
    "from_name": (leaver or {}).get("full_name"),
    "to_name": (taker or {}).get("full_name"),
    "from_status": from_status or "unknown",
    "to_status": to_status or "unknown",
    "from_deactivated": from_deactivated,
    "same_user": same_user,
    "users_seen": len(rows),
}

nodes.code:
# Node 10 - the centrepiece. Of the records about to be handed over, how many
# were edited outside the airlock? Nothing else on the marketplace can ask
# this, because nothing else has scan_changes.
#
# THE JOIN IS BY RECORD, NOT BY OWNER. plan_handover returns counts only - no
# ids - so the leaver's book comes from four read-only COQL nodes instead, one
# per module, using the same "Owner = <id>" filter plan_handover itself uses.
# An owner-based join was the alternative and it is not available either:
# scan_changes puts modified_by in its report FILE, not in changes[], and a
# transform cannot read files.
#
# Effect outputs are flattened by the engine - every list and dict is dropped,
# only scalars survive as top-level keys - so each source is bound as
# {{nodes.X._}} and indexed here.
scan = input.get("scan") or {}
plan = input.get("plan") or {}
changes = scan.get("changes") or []

book = {}
for module, blob in (("Leads", input.get("leads")),
                     ("Contacts", input.get("contacts")),
                     ("Accounts", input.get("accounts")),
                     ("Deals", input.get("deals"))):
    ids = []
    for row in ((blob or {}).get("records") or []):
        if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("id"):
            ids.append(str(row["id"]))
    book[module] = ids

book_size = 0
for module in book:
    book_size = book_size + len(book[module])

overlap = []
per_module = {}
scan_total = 0
for row in changes:
    if not isinstance(row, dict):
        continue
    scan_total = scan_total + 1
    if row.get("governed"):
        continue
    module = str(row.get("module") or "")
    rid = str(row.get("id") or "")
    if not rid or rid not in (book.get(module) or []):
        continue
    per_module[module] = (per_module.get(module) or 0) + 1
    overlap.append({
        "module": module,
        "id": rid,
        "modified_at": row.get("modified_at"),
        "change_ref": row.get("change_ref"),
    })

problems = []
if not changes and scan.get("count"):
    problems.append("scan reported changes but none reached this node")
if book_size == 0:
    problems.append("no records read for the leaver in any module")

# custody_report caps at 500 records per call and takes one module, so node 16
# reports on Leads only. Node 15 covers the rest of the run through the ledger.
leads_ids = (book.get("Leads") or [])[:500]

output = {
    "ok": not problems,
    "problems": problems,
    "overlap_count": len(overlap),
    "overlap": overlap[:200],
    "per_module": per_module,
    "handover_size": plan.get("total") or 0,
    "book_size": book_size,
    "scan_total": scan_total,
    "leads_ids": leads_ids,
    "leads_count": len(leads_ids),
    "basis": "joined by record on module and id: the leaver's book read live "
             "by COQL, intersected with the ungoverned rows scan_changes "
             "returned. Ungoverned EDITS only - a record deleted or merged in "
             "the Zoho UI leaves nothing to poll, so zero overlap is not proof "
             "of a clean book.",
}

# Node 11. Reports a tier. Does NOT enforce one - see below.
#
# Thresholds, written down rather than left as magic numbers:
#   LARGE_BOOK  a reassignment of more than this many records is no longer a
#               routine change; it is most of somebody's portfolio moving at
#               once, and the blast radius of getting the wrong to_user is the
#               whole set.
#   Any ungoverned overlap AT ALL escalates. One record edited outside the
#   airlock in the days before an offboarding is the signal this workflow
#   exists to surface; a threshold above zero would hide exactly the case
#   that matters.
LARGE_BOOK = 100

size = input.get("handover_size") or 0
overlap = input.get("overlap_count") or 0
from_deactivated = bool(input.get("from_deactivated"))
big = size > LARGE_BOOK
reasons = []

if big:
    reasons.append("book of " + str(size) + " records is over the " + str(LARGE_BOOK) + "-record routine threshold")
if overlap:
    reasons.append(str(overlap) + " record(s) in this handover were changed with no approval behind them")
if from_deactivated and overlap:
    reasons.append("the departing user is already deactivated, so those edits were not theirs")

if big and overlap:
    level = "dual_control"
elif big or overlap:
    level = "elevated"
else:
    level = "routine"
    reasons.append("no ungoverned overlap and a book under " + str(LARGE_BOOK) + " records")

output = {
    "level": level,
    "reasons": reasons,
    "requires_second_approver": level == "dual_control",
    "large_book_threshold": LARGE_BOOK,
    "enforced": False,
    "authority": "REPORTED, NOT ENFORCED. The station is the approval "
                 "authority; reaching a real second approver needs team_approval "
                 "and a mesh of separate approvers, which a solo station cannot "
                 "form. This node raises the tier an operator should apply. It "
                 "cannot make the station demand it.",
}
